summary: The main article describes an integrated chemoenzymatic cascade combining nitrilase enzymes with photoredox catalysis to convert nitriles into fluorinated and fluoroalkylated products. The study includes screening of various nitrilases and optimization of photoredox conditions for decarboxylative fluorination, trifluoromethylation, and pentafluoroethylation.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.description: Displays examples of fluorine-containing pharmaceuticals and compares previous integrated chemoenzymatic cascades with the current work's approach for nitrile fluorination.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.description: Screening results of various nitrile substrates against a panel of nitrilases (RrNIT, ReNIT, AfNIT, BjNIT, and NIT014) using both cell-free lysate and whole cells.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.description: Optimization table for decarboxylative fluorination conditions and the structures of the photoredox catalysts used in the study.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.description: Optimization of decarboxylative trifluoromethylation conditions and the resulting substrate scope for the integrated reaction.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.description: Substrate scope for the integrated pentafluoroethylation reaction using hypervalent iodine reagent 3.
